query: Current NIFC IMSR active large fire count for mid-July 2026 (July 11-15), trajectory of national large fire counts and National Preparedness Level
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Summary

**Current status (July 15, 2026 IMSR — most recent):**
- **National Preparedness Level: PL 4** (second-highest on the 1–5 scale)
- **48 uncontained large fires** nationally (the headline "active large fire" count)
- 77 total active incidents in the resource summary (includes contained-but-tracked fires)
- 16,800 personnel assigned, 686,370 acres on active large fires
- Large fires burning in all 10 Geographic Areas

**Trajectory of national large fire counts (mid-July):**
| Date | Uncontained large fires | Personnel | National PL |
|---|---|---|---|
| July 1 | 51 | 9,018 | PL 4 |
| July 8 | 37 | 11,829 | PL 4 |
| July 15 | 48 | 16,800 | PL 4 |

The uncontained fire count **oscillated in the high-30s to low-50s** with no clear monotonic trend, while **personnel assigned rose sharply (+86% over two weeks)** — signaling escalating commitment to increasingly complex fires (led by Rocky Mountain and Great Basin GACCs).

**National Preparedness Level trajectory:**
- PL has held steadily at **PL 4** through all of early-to-mid July 2026
- 2026 escalation path: PL 3 (mid/late June) → PL 4 (late June/early July, coinciding with ~52 fires across 9 states and the fatal Knowles Fire burnover)
- YTD activity running 129–133% (fires) and 132–157% (acres) of the 10-year average

**One important nuance for the caller:** the "active large fire" number can be quoted as either **48** (uncontained — the public/NFN headline figure) or **77** (total incidents in the resource summary), depending on definition. All figures come from authoritative NIFC/NICC IMSR PDFs accessed July 16, 2026. I reported observed data and trajectory only — no forecast.

key_facts: As of the July 15, 2026 IMSR (most recent), NIFC reports 48 uncontained large fires nationally and National Preparedness Level 4 (on a 1-5 scale).

The July 15 IMSR also lists 77 total active incidents in the resource summary; the 48 uncontained figure is the headline 'active large fire' count on NIFC public pages, while 77 includes contained-but-still-tracked incidents.
National Preparedness Level has been at PL 4 continuously through July 1, July 8, and July 15, 2026 (confirmed in each mid-week IMSR).
Trajectory of uncontained large fires: 51 (July 1) -> 37 (July 8) -> 48 (July 15) - oscillating in the high-30s to low-50s with no clear monotonic trend.
Total personnel assigned rose steadily and sharply: 9,018 (July 1) -> 11,829 (July 8) -> 16,800 (July 15), an ~86% increase over two weeks, reflecting escalating resource commitment to complex fires.
On July 15, large fires were burning in all 10 Geographic Area Coordination Centers; Great Basin and Rocky Mountain were at PL 4 (each with 7 uncontained large fires).
Cumulative acres on active large fires: 552,639 (July 1) -> 732,037 (July 8) -> 686,370 (July 15).
Year-to-date fires (39,520) were 129% of the 10-year average and YTD acres (3,633,827) were 132% of the 10-year average as of July 15, 2026.

PL was elevated to PL 3 in mid/late June 2026 and to PL 4 around late June/early July 2026; the PL 4 elevation coincided with ~52 large fires across 9 states and the fatal Knowles Fire firefighter burnover on the Colorado-Utah border.
Minnesota (Superior NF - Camp, Sioux, Bear Trap, Thumb, Wolfpack, Chub) was a national focus area with extreme fire behavior, alongside the drought-stricken West.
